subject: Re: Contract negotiation - penalty & termination terms request
messages:
From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acme.com, bd-team@acme.com
Date: 2026-02-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Service penalties & termination language - contract redline request

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement/legal reviewed the draft and we need stronger remedies in the SLA before legal will sign. High level asks: 

- Fee at risk: 10% of annual committed spend held as "fees at risk" for breach events.
- Liquidated damages: for any calendar month where uptime < 99.5% we want LD equal to 100% of that month's committed spend (applied as invoiced credit or cash).
- Termination: Acme must have unilateral termination rights for material and repeated SLA failures (definition: 3 separate incidents leading to <99.5% in any two consecutive quarters).

I attached a marked-up redline (ACME-requested-redline.pdf) showing the exact language. We know this is not standard, so please escalate if needed — our procurement timeline is tight and this is a gating item for signature.

Appreciate a fast turnaround — Sarah

--
Sarah Lee
Director, Cloud Procurement
Acme Corp
From: priyom.das@redwood.com <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-02-18T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Service penalties & termination language - contract redline request

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for the clear notes and the redline. We absolutely understand Acme's need for reliability guarantees. A few immediate points:

- We cannot agree to cash-style liquidated damages or a pre-funded "fee at risk" that Redwood holds. Our standard remedy is service credits tied to measured downtime; cash payouts or escrowed fees introduce accounting and compliance complexity we don't accept at the platform level.

- Unilateral termination for single or limited incidents is also problematic for us; we prefer a remediation-first path with escalation and mutually agreed termination only after systemic failures.

That said, we want to keep the deal moving. I'm attaching the SLA exhibit we typically offer (SLA-Exhibit-v1.pdf) and proposing a middle ground: enhanced service credits (tiered to severity), a short-term executive SLA review commitment, and a capped "fee exposure" mechanic (not escrowed) that applies only for repeated, unremediated breaches.

I'll loop in Marissa and Rishi from our contracts team to get a concrete counterproposal today. Can you confirm Acme's primary risk threshold (99.5% uptime) and whether your legal team will accept credits capped at a multiple of monthly committed spend instead of cash?

Best,
Priyom
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acme.com, bd-team@acme.com
Date: 2026-02-18T12:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Service penalties & termination language - contract redline request

Priyom —

Appreciate the quick reply. Acme's legal preference is to have an actual financial remedy, not just credits, because of our budgetary rules and audit requirements. If Redwood cannot accept cash LDs, we can consider a certified third-party escrow or a fee-at-risk mechanism (10% holdback paid upon successful completion of the first 6 months).

99.5% is our baseline expectation; we could be persuaded on credits only if the cap is at least 3x monthly committed spend and termination rights exist after repeated systemic failures. Open to Redwood's concrete counter.

-Sarah
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2026-02-19T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Service penalties & termination language - internal alignment

Folks — forwarding Acme's redline and Sarah's follow-ups. Quick internal take so we have negotiated positions ready:

- We should not accept cash liquidated damages or holdbacks. That exposes Redwood to accounting/escrow + tax complexity and sets a bad precedent.
- Workable compromise: accept a written "fee exposure" construct where we agree to increased credits up to a capped cash-equivalent remediation that is payable only if we fail to cure systemic issues after defined remediation windows. Put another way: credits first; if rooted (multi-quarter systemic failure) and remediation fails, then payout triggers up to a capped amount (e.g., 3x MRC).
- Termination: allow limited termination right, but with strict conditions: (a) at least 3 qualified SLA failures within a consecutive 6-month rolling window OR cumulative <99.0% over 30 days; (b) cure periods and remediation playbook exhausted; (c) requirement to migrate workloads safely with 90 days notice and limited wind-down credits.
- Suggest cap on liquidated exposure at 3x monthly committed spend; no escrow; payout only after 60-day cure window and executive sign-off.

I'll draft a redline with that framing (proposed-counterparty-redline.pdf). Rishi, Steph — please weigh in on the commercial/articulation.

—Marissa
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: priyom.das@redwood.com <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2026-02-20T16:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Service penalties & termination language - contract redline request

Sarah —

Thanks for the candor and for surfacing Acme's constraints. Attached is our proposed counter (proposed-counterparty-redline.pdf) — summary of the positions we can accept: 

1) No pre-funded escrow or standard cash liquidated damages.
2) Enhanced service credits as the primary remedy: tiered credits for severity, with credits applied to invoices automatically. Credits are uncapped for individual incidents but we will cap aggregate cash-equivalent exposure for repeated failures at 3x monthly recurring charges (MRC) over any 12-month period.
3) Fee-at-risk alternative: instead of Redwood holding funds, we accept a conditional payout mechanism — if after a 60-day remediation period the failures are determined to be systemic (per the SLA measurement and escalation playbook), Redwood will pay up to the capped exposure amount. Payment requires executive sign-off and third-party verification if requested.
4) Termination rights: Acme may terminate for cause only after (i) three qualified SLA failures in a rolling 6-month window OR (ii) cumulative outage leading to <99.0% over any 30-day window, and only after cure/remediation windows are exhausted. Termination includes a 90-day wind-down and transition support.

This is a compromise to meet Acme's need for accountable remedies while limiting Redwood's exposure and operational risk. If Acme requires an escrow, we can discuss a customer-managed escrow arrangement as a last resort but prefer the payout-upon-failure approach above.

Please review the attached redline and let me know if we can iterate quickly — our aim is to close the SOW and start onboarding in March.

Best regards,
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: proposed-counterparty-redline.pdf
